what_it_does: LLM-based speech recognition (transcribing audio to text with large language models) is slow because generating each word requires the previous word, creating a serial bottleneck. SpecASR accelerates this through speculative decoding: use a fast small model to guess the next few words (speculate), then verify in parallel with the accurate large model. The key insight specific to speech: the small and large models' outputs stay aligned (they agree on what word comes next), so speculative guesses succeed more often. SpecASR adapts how many words to guess dynamically, recycles previous guesses when possible, and uses smart token-tree generation to balance latencies between the two models.
